spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: V. You came. I was expecting a polite refusal and a malware scan.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Somebody stole Heartbreaker Protocol. I built it to break emotional-conditioning loops. The Claws turned it into a weapon. Now they're selling it.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: The original interrupts conditioning signals. Gives people a window to say no. Theirs keeps the signal screaming until the nervous system folds.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Their build has the only live signing key. Burn it and I can't revoke the copies. Recover first. Patch second. Dramatic explosions a distant third.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Only the critical ones. Low-priority tickets get a tasteful wink.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Three Claws, two access points. Recover my code and its signing key from the first. Then use the second to shut down the stolen copies. Keep both boxes intact.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: And if you see little black bows in the interface, those are mine. Extremely important diagnostic equipment.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: I'll be here. Pretending this is a normal amount of anxiety.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: That's the operation. Recovery point first. Keep it intact; I need the code, not a smoking case.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Of course they are. Turn off the safety and call it a subscription.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: No. Read the revoke instructions. We'll talk about the rest when you're clear.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Copy the prototype and its signing key. That key lets us shut down the stolen copies.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Good. Upload my fix at the second access point. It'll shut down the stolen copies and give the guards a few seconds of optical trouble.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Fits in the menu. Very professional.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Fix accepted. Stolen copies shut down. Oh, look. Hearts. And the bows survived compilation.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: The guards' optics will recover. The people they sold this to get their emotions back. Now get clear.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Link dropped. Nothing committed. Reconnect when you're ready.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: There you are. Code intact. Distribution keys dead. I almost sent a normal thank-you.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: A friend. Her partner paid for a mood regulator. Called it helping. Every time she got angry, it made being agreeable feel better.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: She knew something was wrong. Just couldn't hold on to the feeling long enough to leave.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: I wanted to give her that feeling back. Not put another one in its place.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: She did the leaving. I just broke a lock. Still... thanks for knowing the difference.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: People remember hearts. And the ribbons are black. There are standards.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: She's out. We talk when she wants. Sometimes she doesn't. That's sort of the point.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Your own build. Heartbreaker Protocol. Velvet Crash on the quickhack menu. No conditioning payload. Just a short combat-system interruption and terrible taste.

spoken_lines.speaker: Velvet
spoken_lines.text: Don't sound so brave. They suit you.
